_meta.purpose: Program-membership overrides for data/atlas/hotel/luxury-hotels.json. The feed carries the channel a property was imported under (nearly always 'Virtuoso'), which collapses whole hotel-company programs into one bucket. Each rule here promotes a family of properties onto the program that actually governs them, so the atlas's 'Brand / Program' axis and the preferred-partner ranking see the real relationship.
_meta.editingRule: Never hand-edit program/brand in luxury-hotels.json — a re-import would silently drop it. Add a rule here instead; both consumers apply this file at load, so the override survives a feed refresh.
_meta.matching: A hotel joins a rule when its `brand` equals a brandRule's `brand` (case/accent-insensitive) OR its `name` matches that rule's `namePattern`. Patterns are anchored on word boundaries so they cannot match mid-word ('Regent' never matches 'Regency'). `excludeIds` wins over everything.

fieldsWritten.program: set to the rule's program name
fieldsWritten.brand: set to the brandRule's brand — fills the many IHG records the feed left null, and corrects a mislabelled one (see notes)
fieldsWritten.programSource: the feed's original program value, preserved so nothing is lost

notes: IHG's luxury & lifestyle agency program. Membership is by IHG brand, so the rule set below IS the definition of the category.
The Virtuoso amenities these properties carry (vipUpgrades) are unchanged — they are delivered through this program; only the program label moves.

h_00983 InterContinental Danang Sun Peninsula Resort was labelled brand 'The Peninsula' / program 'The Peninsula Pen Club' in the feed. The 'Peninsula' in its name is the Son Tra peninsula, not The Peninsula Hotels — it is an IHG InterContinental, so this rule corrects both fields.

The Virtuoso feed lists Auberge properties as '<Name>, Auberge Collection' under program 'Virtuoso', so the atlas's Auberge filter showed only the handful of base records that happened to carry the program. The name suffix is the membership signal.
Matched by name only, not brand: the feed tags three unrelated hotels with brand 'Auberge Resorts' because 'Auberge' is in their names. They are excluded below so the brand test cannot pull them in.
h_00159 Auberge du Jeu de Paume (Chantilly) and h_00156 Auberge Saint-Antoine (Québec) are Relais & Châteaux houses, not Auberge Resorts.
h_01091 L'Auberge Del Mar is not an Auberge Resorts property (Virtuoso's chain field says Noble House). It is excluded here; its base program is left for a person to correct.

Keyed to Virtuoso's own chain field. The feed files every one of these under the import channel 'Virtuoso', so the program's atlas filter showed only the few base records that carried the label (most of them photo-less stubs). Only hotels still on 'Virtuoso' move; a hotel already filed under a specific program keeps it.
